title: Conditionals — typing drills
description: Type if, elif, and match lines the horror systems will use. Spacing is flexible, and a trailing semicolon is fine.

drills.prompt: Write an if line that checks whether fear is greater than 80.0.
drills.hint: if, then the comparison, then a colon at the end of the line.
drills.explain: This is the panic branch. When fear creeps past 80, the body under this if will run.

drills.prompt: Write an if line that is true only when mic_volume is greater than threshold and distance is less than or equal to hear_distance.
accepted: if mic_volume > threshold and distance <= hear_distance:
if mic_volume > threshold and distance <= hear_distance :
drills.hint: Use and so both sides must be true. End the line with a colon.
drills.explain: and means both sides must be true. The monster hears you only if you are loud enough and close enough.

drills.prompt: Write an if line that runs when the flashlight is off, using the variable is_flashlight_on.
drills.hint: not flips a bool. If the light is off, is_flashlight_on is false.
drills.explain: not is_flashlight_on is true when the flashlight is off. The ! prefix is also valid in GDScript.

drills.prompt: Write an elif line that checks whether stamina is less than or equal to 0.0.
drills.hint: Use elif, not a second if, and end the line with a colon.
drills.explain: elif is the next branch in a chain. It runs only when the if above it was false and this condition is true.

drills.prompt: Write the fallback branch line in a match statement.
drills.hint: It is a single underscore, then a colon. It works like else.
drills.explain: The _ branch is the safety net in a match. It runs when the value did not match any named branch above it.
